finalText:
Redis crashed at 02:14:07, and the system spiraled from there.

When Redis went down on `10.0.0.12:6379`, the cache layer fell back to direct database reads. Without the cache, every request hit the store. The store couldn't handle the load — requests started timing out within seconds. As timeouts piled up, the request queue backed up past its 500-item limit to 562, then 568. The app kept buffering more requests while waiting for the store, and by 02:31:44 (17 minutes later) the heap ran out of memory. Worker-2 crashed, then the whole API became unresponsive and was killed.

Redis tried to reconnect 12 times but couldn't reach the server. The system had no circuit breaker or backpressure mechanism to fail fast — it just queued requests forever until memory was gone.
